eligibility: Applicant is a tenured associate or full professor (Principal Investigator)
Project is carried out at a Finnish university
Project is innovative and pioneering research in Information and Communications Technologies (ICT)
Proposal has the potential to open genuinely new research frontiers
existing.eligibility_summary: A tenured associate or full professor at a Finnish university submits the application as Principal Investigator for their own ICT research project. The grant finances the salary of a doctoral or postdoctoral researcher hired onto that project.
benefits: Researcher position to be hired on the project
Possible extension via the following year's application process
coverage: EUR 75,000 to finance hiring a doctoral or postdoctoral researcher
Financial plan must break the grant down between the researcher's salary, overheads and possible other expenses
requirements: Project led by a tenured associate or full professor acting as their own project's Principal Investigator
Project carried out at a Finnish university
Each professor may submit only one application per call
Ethical and research security aspects of the research comprehensively explained in the application form
documents: Clear, concise and realistic project plan, with no length restriction and no official template
Detailed financial plan breaking the grant down across salary, overhead costs and possible other expenses
Explanation of ethical and research security aspects of the research
Information on the researcher to be hired, if already identified
application_method: Submit through the Nokia Foundation electronic grant application system; drafts can be saved and completed later
existing.selection_notes: The Foundation asks applicants to clearly highlight the innovativeness and the high-risk high-reward nature of the proposed project. Grant decisions for the 2026 call are scheduled for late October 2026.
existing.best_fit: Tenured associate or full professors at Finnish universities who want to recruit a doctoral or postdoctoral researcher onto a genuinely new, high-risk ICT research direction.
existing.notes: Successful projects may begin in early 2027 and must conclude no later than August 2028. Successful applicants may reapply for an extension through the following year's application process.
existing.deadline_display: "Call for applications is open from 18 May 2026 to 15 September 2026." That 2026 call closed before this verification on 2026-10-04; the call recurs annually.

eligibility: Postdoctoral researcher or younger tenure-track scholar at assistant professor level
Research relates to ICT, potentially bridging social, behavioural, economics and service sciences
Research supports and promotes education and research within Finland
Research falls within one of the three Jorma Ollila Fund focus areas
existing.eligibility_summary: Postdoctoral researchers and younger tenure-track scholars at assistant professor level in Finnish universities, whose research is in Information and Communications Technologies or a supporting discipline, and who need funding for a research visit abroad to gain international experience.
benefits: Funding for a research visit of 0.5 to 3 years at a host organisation abroad
Access to the Nokia Foundation contact network
Possibility to defer the start of an awarded grant by one year
coverage: Up to EUR 30,000 for a 12-month visit, up to EUR 50,000 with exceptionally good justification such as family travel
Costs of the visit, not the grantee's salary
Proportionally smaller amounts for visits shorter than a year
requirements: Invitation letter from the academic host must be included in the application
Report on the progress of any previous or ongoing grant for second and third year applications
Pre-examiners' statements on the thesis where the applicant has official permission to defend
Research must comply with the charter of the Nokia Foundation
documents: Invitation letter from the academic host of the visit
Progress report on any previous or ongoing Jorma Ollila grant, for second and third year applications
Pre-examiners' statements on the thesis, where the applicant has official permission to defend
application_method: Submit through the Nokia Foundation grant system; drafts can be saved and completed later
existing.selection_notes: The Foundation recommends applying for a grant for a visit with one host organisation and for a period of one year. Grants are given for a maximum of one year at a time and for a maximum of three years in total.
existing.best_fit: Postdocs and assistant professors at Finnish universities in ICT who need 0.5 to 3 years of funding for a single research visit abroad.
existing.notes: The three focus areas are Data Science and AI, Wireless and Network Technologies, and Future Microelectronics.
existing.deadline_display: Applications can be submitted twice a year. For 2026: the spring call ran from 2 March until 17 April 2026 as part of the Tutkijat maailmalle programme, and the autumn call was open "from 3 August until 15 September 2026". Both 2026 deadlines have passed.
existing.program_type: Postdoctoral and tenure-track research visit grant
